data.title: Rogers Sugar: Hold as Stable Outlook and Limited Near-Term Catalysts Offset Sound Demand
data.description:
Analyst Stephen Macleod of BMO Capital maintained a Hold rating on Rogers Sugar, with a price target of C$7.50.

Stephen Macleod has given his Hold rating due to a combination of factors, including results that were broadly consistent with expectations and an outlook suggesting limited change in performance during 2027. Sugar operations face modest volume pressure, the reversal of temporary margin benefits, competitive domestic conditions, and weaker export demand, while Maple Products is expected to deliver largely stable volumes and profitability.
Although underlying sweetener demand remains sound and the dividend may appeal to income-focused investors, these positives appear largely reflected in Rogers Sugar’s current valuation. The company also faces uncertainty from U.S. trade negotiations and possible tariff-related effects, while the LEAP project will not be completed until 2027 and requires a longer ramp-up, limiting near-term catalysts.

Macleod covers the Consumer Cyclical sector, focusing on stocks such as Groupe Dynamite Inc., Gildan Activewear, and Aritzia. According to TipRanks, Macleod has an average return of 17.1% and a 61.07% success rate on recommended stocks.

In another report released today, Desjardins also downgraded the stock to a Hold with a C$7.50 price target.

data.title: Salesforce’s AI Expansion and Accelerating Growth Support Buy Rating; Price Target Unchanged at $266
data.description:
Monness analyst Brian White has maintained their bullish stance on CRM stock, giving a Buy rating today.

Brian White gave his Buy rating based on several factors, including Salesforce’s expanding role in enterprise AI and its broad cloud product portfolio. New offerings such as AIforce, along with integrations involving Microsoft and Slack, could help the company capture demand as customers build more agent-driven operations. He also points to a substantial acquisition program that broadens Salesforce’s capabilities and market reach.
White expects Salesforce to deliver third-quarter revenue of about $11.541 billion and EPS of $3.46, modestly ahead of consensus. His forecast calls for revenue growth to accelerate to 12% year over year, while subscription and support revenue rises 13%, indicating improving momentum. With the price target unchanged at $266, these prospects support the Buy view despite difficult software conditions and a challenging macroeconomic backdrop.

In another report released today, J.P. Morgan also maintained a Buy rating on the stock with a $265.00 price target.
